correctness.rationale: The normalized 2x2 Pauli basis yields |q|^2+a+b+c=2, with a,b<=1. For 0<|q|<1 every point (a,1+s^2-a), s^2<=a<=1, is realized by a determinant-zero, Hilbert–Schmidt-norm-one rank-one matrix having trace |q|. Thus the two-variable maximization has exactly the full attained top edge and no relaxation gap. Maximization of alpha^p a^(p/2)+beta^p(T-a)^(p/2) is strictly concave for 1<=p<2 with the stated critical point and endpoint transition, affine at p=2, strictly convex for p>2, and has radius alpha at p=infinity. Equality classifications distinguish finite p from infinity, including alpha=beta. Standard-library diagnostics passed 11997 sampled assertions; universal correctness rests on the proof.

originality.rationale: Comparisons were made at the level of objects, quantifiers and implications. The 2026 Azadi theorem supplies general topological properties and a unit-overlap realization, not a sharp weighted p-norm optimization at interior q. Feki et al. supply general inequalities and unrelated nonconvex 2x2 examples; Theorem 17 is a nonsharp block upper bound. Xu et al. concern ordinary state expectations, not fixed overlap between two distinct vectors. Related index records concern weighted projection pairs at q=1, rank-one q numerical radii, or commuting fields. None inspected states or logically implies the exact three-parameter crossover without the additional Pauli allocation-saturation computation. Generalized Clifford/orbitope priority remains a live risk.
residual_risks: A classical C-numerical-range, two-by-two Clifford/Pauli orbitope, or constrained trace-norm result may imply this weighted optimization without naming joint q-numerical radii.
Generic all-p sharp tuple norm results not indexed under Pauli or q-overlap terminology could contain the same formula.
The checks are same-model literature comparisons, not independent publication-priority verification.

value.rationale: The fixed-overlap joint q-radius is a natural operator invariant for a canonical noncommuting Hermitian pair. Complete exact dependence on overlap, the norm exponent and unequal weights reveals a sharp, explicitly located transition between an interior balanced extremizer and saturation of the stronger observable; the crossover cannot be seen in unweighted p=2 inequalities or ordinary q=1 Pauli geometry. The result is a complete natural finite-dimensional classification and a quantitative benchmark for general q-tuple inequalities, not an arbitrary numerical instance.
